wp6_5_finish_session_102.summary: WP6.5 finish landed — Provider.put / parseLegacyPut / getService natives populate a per-provider serviceMap so Cipher.getInstance(algo, providerName) and Signature.getInstance(algo, providerName) can resolve registered services. See native-builtins/src/jca/provider_chain.rs (parse_legacy_key, apply_legacy_put, ServiceMap, provider_put_native, provider_parse_legacy_put_native, provider_get_service_native, provider_service_get_class_name) + tests in vm/tests/wp6_5_finish_provider_chain_resolution.rs (4/4) and the new unit pins in jca::provider_chain::tests (12 added → 20/20 total).
wp6_5_finish_session_102.scope_decision: Full BC <clinit> integration end-to-end (loading bcprov-jdk18on.jar and exercising real BC AES-GCM through the chain) requires the BC jar at runtime, which the rust-jvm fixture deliberately doesn't ship as a build dependency. The mechanics of the chain (population by put/parseLegacyPut, resolution by getService, Service object construction via the session-101 <init> shim) are pinned at the unit level. Closure of the actual BC bytecode boot is tracked as WP6.5b — see known_blockers below.
wp6_5_finish_session_102.next_failure_surface: When BC's actual <clinit> runs against the populated serviceMap, the next surface is likely either (a) a class-loading gap in BC's reflective SPI instantiation pathway (`Class.forName(svc.getClassName()).newInstance()`), or (b) a real-bytecode interaction between Hashtable.put and our Provider.put native that the unit tests don't exercise (mock heap doesn't run inherited bytecode). Watch for NoClassDefFoundError on org.bouncycastle.* in the bcprobe stderr.
